paragraphs.text: [PDF page 1] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires David Orkin Candidate's Full Name David Orkin Candidate's Pronouns he/him Do you identify as a member of the LGBTQ community? If so, please specify as you are comfortable* Yes. I am running as an openly gay man on a pro-LGBTQ+ platform. I have roots in the local queer community through organizing, social circles, and arts communities in my home neighborhood of Ridgewood. Office New York State Assembly District Number 38 Full Name of Campaign Committee(s) David for Queens 2026d Campaign Website https://www.david4queens.com/ Campaign Social Media Handles Instagram: @david4queens | X: @david4queens | Bluesky: @david4queens.com | Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/share/18AhiMHTAy/?mibextid=wwXIfr If endorsed will you display the endorsement of the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC in your literature whenever you list other endorsements, including on your campaign website? If no, please explain. I’ll proudly feature the Stonewall Democratic Club of NYS endorsement on my website, social media, and anywhere else it makes strategic sense to promote it. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you are seeking? NYers just made history by electing Zohran Mamdani as mayor, demanding a more affordable, dignified future that puts working people over the wealthy. In AD-38, Dem primary voters backed Zohran by 40 points, delivering a clear mandate for the district. But he needs allies in Albany to carry out that mandate. As an immigrant workers’ rights attorney, the son of an immigrant mother, a fluent Spanish speaker, a union organizer, and an openly gay man, I’m running to bring this movement to Albany. Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 1

[PDF page 2] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ movement. Please be specific. My commitment to the LGBTQ movement has been a through-line in both my professional life and personal life. As a queer person who has been working in the immigrant rights movement for over a decade, I have always prioritized a queer perspective in my work: when I was organizing in the U.S.–Mexico borderlands in my early 20s, I became involved with Mariposas Sin Fronteras, an Arizona-based organization supporting queer and trans migrants in detention centers across Central Arizona. I also worked in a migrant shelter in Ixtepec, Oaxaca, Mexico, that provided services and HIV/AIDS healthcare for LGBTQ+ migrants. These experiences at the border inspired me to pursue a law degree so I could offer tangible support to movements for justice and queer liberation. As an attorney at MRNY, I’ve had the privilege of working with many LGBTQ+ clients in uniquely precarious situations. My clientele has included queer and trans immigrant workers who have suffered employment discrimination, sexual harassment, and persistent wage theft. As part of this work, I have lobbied the New York City Council for increased funding to the NYC Commission on Human Rights. I deeply admire GLITS, a Black trans-led advocacy organization that provides housing for queer residents in need at its Woodhaven facility in-district. I had the honor of meeting with GLITS’ founder, Ceyenne, to learn more about their needs, and I look forward to partnering with her and members of the organization in their individual capacities to support this campaign. My campaign is also supported by leaders from the Caribbean Equality Project, a local advocacy group for Afro- and Indo-Caribbean queer communities. Our forthcoming policy platform on LGBTQ+ issues and reproductive rights is developed in close collaboration with organizers from these communities as well as NYC-DSA’s Trans Rights and Bodily Autonomy campaign, and informed by my experience as an out queer man. My personal favorite LGBTQ+ event in NYC every year is the Trans-Latinx march with MRNY— I bring many friends who wouldn’t normally go to Corona Plaza to come out and celebrate the trans immigrant community. For immigrant communities, especially queer immigrant communities, it is crucial to have mass support when publicly protesting the policies that oppress their families, because there is safety in numbers. I have also served as a legal observer for these actions. But I also know that across all our differences, working people--including LGBTQ+ people--fundamentally need the same things: dignity, security, and joy in our workplaces, in our homes, and in our communities. We deserve quality public education, childcare, and healthcare, beautiful public spaces, and reliable, affordable public transit. We deserve a vacation. At MRNY, my coworkers trusted me enough to elect me to the bargaining committee of our union, UAW Local 2320 (NOLSW), representing more than 100 workers. I helped secure our first contract, winning $10,000+ raises for the lowest-paid staff, a free healthcare option, and a 35-hour workweek. I saw firsthand how these gains, won through our collective power, transformed people’s lives. This is the same fight I’ll bring to Albany for working-class and LGBTQ+ New Yorkers in AD-38 and across the state. What are your policy priorities if you are to win this seat? How will these policy priorities impact the LGBTQ community? Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 2

[PDF page 3] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires My policy priorities are rooted in the belief that queer liberation is inseparable from economic and racial justice. In AD-38, our community’s safety is threatened not just by bigoted rhetoric, but by material crises like housing instability, healthcare exclusion, and state-sanctioned violence. My top priority is taxing the rich to fund an affordable New York. By passing the full Invest in Our New York (IONY) legislative package, we can generate the revenue needed to decommodify housing and guarantee healthcare. LGBTQ+ New Yorkers, particularly our youth and elders, are disproportionately impacted by poverty and displacement; taxing the billionaire class is the only way to build a social safety net that ensures no one is forced to choose between their identity and a roof over their head. Secondly, I will fight to protect our immigrant neighbors from ICE. Queer and trans immigrants face double the vulnerability in our carceral system, where detention can be a death sentence for those denied gender-affirming care or safety from abuse. I will champion the New York for All Act and the Dignity Not Detention Act to end local collusion with federal deportation and ensure New York is a true sanctuary for all. Finally, I am committed to expanding workers’ rights. As a member of the coalition fighting for the EmPIRE Act, I know that economic power is the best defense against discrimination, and unionized workers have more protections on the job. Workplace exploitation often targets the most marginalized; by giving workers the tools to hold bad bosses accountable, we empower LGBTQ+ workers to demand the dignity and safety they deserve. Please list here the union, organizations (community, civic, media, issue groups), LGBTQ leaders, and elected officials that have endorsed you. Organizations: NYC-DSA, NY WFP, UAW Region 9A, Desis Rising Up and Moving (DRUM) Beats, Make the Road Action NY (MRA NY), Churches United for Fair Housing (CUFFH) Action, TenantsPAC, TREEAge, Hindus for Human Rights (HFHR) Action, Organization of Staff Analysts (OSA) Union, Office & Professional Employees International Union (OPEIU) Local 153, Citizen Action NY, NY Progressive Action Network (NYPAN) Elected officials: NYC Council Members Alexa Avilés, Tiffany Cabán, Chi Ossé, Shahana Hanif, Jennifer Gutiérrez, Sandy Nurse; NYS Assembly Members Claire Valdez, Emily Gallagher, Diana Moreno, and Sarahana Shrestha, NYS Senators Kristen Gonzalez, Julia Salazar, and Jabari Brisport. Have you ever endorsed any LGBTQ candidates? Which ones? I am not an incumbent so I have not endorsed anyone. Would you in the future endorse, appoint or financially support any candidate for public office, elected official, or political appointee with a record of opposing LGBTQ equality? If yes, please explain. * No Across the nation, and in New York State, we have seen a massive wave of anti LGBTQ legislation, including restricting the rights of trans youth, bans on LGBTQ books in schools, limits on drag queen performances, and limits on gender affirming care for minors and adults. How would you use your platform as a New York State Legislator to advocate for the protection of LGBTQ people across the city, state, and country? Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 3

[PDF page 4] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires The LGBTQ+ community, and especially the trans community, is living through a deeply uncertain time under the current federal administration. Civil liberties, social acceptance, and the agencies that enforce our anti-discrimination laws, hard won through struggle, are being challenged and in some cases rolled back. Reactionary political forces are weaponizing our identities, especially those of trans people, as a wedge issue to fracture working class solidarity. Bodily autonomy and reproductive rights are under attack in ways that profoundly harm queer and trans people here in AD-38 and across the state and nation. New York has long been a haven for the LGBTQ+ community across the country and around the world, with many queer people like myself coming here in search of safety and networks of support. I plan to use my power in Albany to ensure the city and state can provide the protection and support we need. I wholeheartedly support initiatives to defend the LGBTQ+ community, including strong protections against discrimination, and I will fight every effort to restrict gender-affirming care. I will use my office to stand with my LGBTQ+ community on the Assembly floor and through my public bully pulpit. I will support trans sanctuary legislation like the Gender Identity Respect, Dignity, and Safety (GIRDS) Act (S1049A / A5478A), whose Assembly and Senate bill authors have both endorsed my campaign. By contrast, the incumbent has been called out by a leader of the Repeal Walking While Trans Ban coalition for misleadingly taking credit for this initiative: https://x.com/Brianr4NY/status/2025751790596055385. I also believe my top priorities in Albany — including the affordability agenda, protecting our communities from ICE, and stronger labor protections — will address and intersect with the issues faced by the LGBTQ+ community in NYC. Even though all workers, tenants, and immigrants will benefit from increased protections on the state level, for example, these issues are experienced in more profoundly harmful ways by LGBTQ+ workers, tenants, and immigrants. I am committed to bringing an intersectional perspective to each of these issues to my legislative office. The LGBTQ community has historically been overpoliced, and research shows that law enforcement continues to disproportionately target marginalized people: What do you view as the New York State Legislature's role in ensuring law enforcement oversight, funding, and role in meeting the needs of marginalized communities? What, if any, relevant policy proposals do you support regarding law enforcement? My vision for public safety is Care, Not Cages. I believe true public safety is achieved through deep community investments that address the issues making our communities less safe. By taxing the rich to fund the social services our communities need and deserve, we can make real progress toward addressing the underlying drivers of crime. I support Mayor Mamdani’s proposal for a Department of Community Safety, which is already being implemented in concept—one that prevents violence by deploying civilian mental health professionals to respond to mental health crises so police aren’t tasked with handling mental health emergencies. I also believe strongly in civilian oversight of police, and I believe that police departments should be subject to the oversight of civilian complaint review boards with the final say in police discipline. I support the legislation Holding Police Accountable by Strengthening the Civilian Complaint Review Board (S4354 Bailey / A126 Cruz) to that effect, which broadens the CCRB’s authority to investigate bias-based policing, which disproportionately impacts LGBTQ+ people and other marginalized communities. New York State is experiencing a housing crisis, and the LGBTQ community disproportionately experiences homelessness, especially our LGBTQ youth and seniors. How do you intend to ensure that any housing plan is Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC — 2026 State Legislature Questionnaire Page 4

[PDF page 5] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires equitable to the LGBTQ Community and other marginalized groups? I believe that housing is a human right. On the issue of homelessness, which disproportionately impacts the LGBTQ+ community and other marginalized communities, my thoughts are the following. I would not oppose shelters in AD-38 for homeless NYers–or asylum seekers, for that matter. I would support making permanent and fully funding the Housing Access Voucher Program to provide housing for the currently homeless, and those at risk of losing their homes. I would also support A108 / S113, which would provide an increased monthly cash allowance for individuals and families residing in shelters. Especially as we just experienced a brutal winter that puts homeless people at extreme risk, I would co-sponsor the Winter Moratorium on Evictions Bill to stop preventable deaths by cold exposure for New Yorkers struggling to afford their housing. I would also support the expansion of supportive housing for residents in need of mental health treatment, addiction recovery, disability care, or other medical services. At the same time, we must invest in the housing we already have. Public housing is the only form of permanently affordable housing at scale, yet the state has allowed it to deteriorate. I support fully funding NYCHA with billions in direct state capital investment to repair boilers, fix elevators, remediate mold, and address the unacceptable conditions residents face. I oppose any effort to privatize NYCHA. As a longer-term initiative, I would champion the Social Housing Development Authority (SHDA) Act (A6265/S5674), which would establish a public developer to build permanently affordable social housing, including co-ops and programs like Mitchell-Lama. This model would ensure high labor standards by requiring prevailing wages or project labor agreements for construction and building services. Social housing is resident-controlled, permanently affordable, and insulated from speculation and market volatility. It ensures that New Yorkers can remain in their communities and have a right to shape the future of their own homes. Ultimately, the cornerstone of an agenda that supports homeless and low-income New Yorkers must be a tax-the-rich revenue plan to fully fund the services they need. In today’s political climate, what role should the New York Legislature play in protecting and expanding access to comprehensive reproductive and gender-affirming healthcare? Will you commit to defending access to abortion care and gender-affirming care for both adults and youth, including taking legislative action to prevent hospitals and healthcare systems—such as NYU Langone Health—from restricting or ending lifesaving care due to political pressure or federal intimidation? * Recently, NYU Langone, one of New York City’s major hospital networks, announced it would end its gender affirming care program for minors, citing the “current regulatory environment.” This anticipatory obedience, voluntarily complying in advance with the Trump administration, is not only cowardly but ignores the real harm done to trans youth. Time and again, when institutions bend to authoritarianism instead of standing up for what is right, it only invites further challenges and erosion of protections. I stand with the protestors who demanded that NYU Langone reverse this decision, and in office, I will amplify these calls to action and use every available lever of power at my disposal to reverse the harmful restrictions of care. We are also in a moment of crisis for abortion access, and this has only worsened since the Supreme Court overturned nearly 50 years of precedent and eliminated the federal constitutional right to abortion. [PDF page 6] Stonewall Democratic Club of NYC 2026 State Legislature Questionnaires lawmakers to pass and enforce laws that restrict reproductive freedom, with devastating impacts across the country. As of June 2025, bans on some or all abortions are being enforced in more than 20 states. In 2025, a Louisiana court indicted New York doctor Margaret Carpenter for allegedly providing abortion pills to a Louisiana resident, and we can expect these harrowing legal attacks to mount in the years ahead. But New Yorkers are fighting back. In 2024, voters overwhelmingly passed an Equal Rights Amendment enshrining in our state constitution critical protections against discrimination based on pregnancy, pregnancy outcomes, reproductive health care, and autonomy. We have also continued to advance legislation that protects patients and providers seeking, assisting, and delivering this essential care. In office, I will support this critical work. Privacy Amendment S8603 (Ramos) / A9377 (Shimsky) This amendment would enshrine a fundamental right to privacy in the New York Constitution, protecting personal decisions, bodily autonomy, and limiting government surveillance beyond federal standards. It is especially critical for LGBTQ+ New Yorkers whose sensitive data could otherwise be misused or weaponized. Yes Comprehensive Sex Education (CSE) S6901A (Salazar) / A7496 (Gonzalez-Rojas) This bill ensures age-appropriate, inclusive sex education statewide that reflects national standards. It reduces stigma, affirms LGBTQ+ students, and promotes safer, more informed school environments. Yes New York for All Act S2235 (Gounardes) / A3506 (Reyes) This bill limits state and local involvement in immigration enforcement, protecting immigrant families and public safety. It is vital for safeguarding LGBTQ+ immigrants who face heightened risks of targeting and discrimination. Yes Holding Police Accountable by Strengthening the Civilian Complaint Review Board S4354 (Bailey) / A126 (Cruz) This act expands the CCRB’s authority to investigate bias-based policing, which disproportionately harms LGBTQ+ people, particularly LGBTQ+ New Yorkers of color. It is a necessary step toward real accountability and trust in law enforcement. Yes The Gender Identity Respect Dignity and Safety Act (GIRDS) (A5478A - Gallagher/ S1049A Salazar) This bill ensures incarcerated transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals are treated with dignity, respected in placement, and provided gender-affirming necessities. It significantly improves safety and reduces abuse in correctional settings. Yes A6059 (Simone) / S03227 (Hoylman - Sigal) Prohibits health insurers, health care plans and HMOs from requiring prior authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis used to prevent HIV infection Yes The Freedom to Read Act S8630 (May) / A9537 (Simone) This bill prevents book bans based on LGBTQ+ identity or family structure in schools and libraries.
